prompt: In GitHub flow, why is each change built on its own short-lived branch?
explanation: GitHub flow keeps the default branch always shippable; topic branches isolate one idea each so review stays small and merges stay safe. Git does not forbid direct commits — that is a convention (later enforced with branch protection).

options.text: The default branch stays deployable, and each branch carries one reviewable idea
Branches are required because Git forbids committing to the default branch
Short branches use less storage on GitHub
Every branch automatically deploys to production
